Team — forwarding Medicenta's asks. Short summary: 20% one-time ramp discount for 6 months; legal wants a broader hold-harmless carveout touching clinical data processing. Jared's redlines tweak indemnity and expand warranty exceptions.

My read: 20% one-time is near the top of what comp can approve (we typically top out at 15% for ramp cases). The legal change is material — it shifts risk to Redwood for categories we shouldn't accept without either a liability cap carveback or explicit exclusions for gross negligence and willful misconduct.

Please advise next steps and who needs to be looped for exec clearance. If this goes to approval, suggest the following alternatives to offer Medicenta:
- Accept 15% one-time ramp discount (instead of 20%) and offer credit-based milestone payments to mitigate cash exposure.
- Counter legal: preserve standard indemnity; add narrow carveout language limited to third-party claims arising from customer-supplied datasets and explicit consented research workflows.

Markus / Aditya — can you weigh in on the SLA/credit side? Marissa — would legal be comfortable with the narrow carveout + an explicit $5M liability exception tied to proven breach scenarios?

Olga
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Team — per my review: the hold-harmless expansion in Medicenta's SOW materially increases Redwood's exposure for categories we cannot carve back through contract alone (it attempts to shift liability for regulatory claims tied to customer clinical data). Legal will not accept the proposed sweeping carveout.

Proposed path for exec clearance (recommended, concise):
1) Commercial: Approve a promotional credit equivalent to a 20% ramp discount for months 1–6 (credit applied to invoices as a one-off line item). This preserves our pricing guardrails and gives Medicenta the commercial uplift they requested.
2) Risk/Legal: Reject their broad hold-harmless. Offer a narrowly scoped hold-harmless for (a) direct clinical integration activities where data was supplied by Medicenta and (b) claims tied solely to Medicenta's misuse of customer-supplied datasets.
3) Liability cap: Approve an exception to the standard $2M cap to $5M limited solely to breaches caused by Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct; all other categories remain under the standard cap.

If Sales approves, please confirm and I will prepare the exact redline language for the SOW/MSA and a single-slide summary for the exec signature (we should aim for sign-off from Ravi or the CFO). We need a short note explaining the business rationale (board timing, expected ARR, strategic reference customer).

Attachments: Medicenta_MSA_risk_matrix.xlsx

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
